pageTitle: Klacks for Hospitality & Food Service in Saudi Arabia | 9-Hour Rule & Night Shifts Scheduled

hero.titleHtml: Early, late, night shifts — the 9-hour rule under control.
hero.subtitle: Klacks schedules front of house, kitchen, and housekeeping under Saudi labour law — including the 9-hour normal working time for the hospitality sector (Ministerial Decision 2836/1/1427), the 11-hour daily attendance cap (Art. 101), and the night window from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. (MD 18632/1441).
hero.screenshotAlt: Klacks timeline view for shift schedules in hospitality and food service

items.title: Making use of the 9-hour normal working time
items.text: The hospitality sector may schedule 9 instead of 8 hours of normal working time (MD 2836/1/1427) — while Art. 101 caps daily attendance at 11 hours. Split shifts thus remain effectively tightly constrained.

items.title: Ramadan planning
items.text: During Ramadan, weekly working time for Muslim employees drops to 36 hours (Art. 98) — while Iftar and Suhoor business often means peak season. Reconciling both is the real art of scheduling.

items.title: Night work with special rules
items.text: The night window runs from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. (MD 18632/1441) — and night workers need at least 12 hours of rest. Anyone closing late can't open early again — at least not with the same staff.

solutions.title: How Klacks lightens the load for hospitality
solutions.subtitle: From the early shift to the night shift — it all works together.

items.title: 9-hour rule & 11-hour cap planned cleanly
items.text: The 9-hour normal working time and the 11-hour attendance cap (Art. 101) can be stored as rules — every breach is flagged immediately.

items.title: Ramadan season planned
items.text: Klacks factors the reduced 36-hour weekly budget during Ramadan (Art. 98) into planning — shift lengths and staffing adjust without quietly generating overtime.

items.title: Weekly rest secured
items.text: A maximum of 6 consecutive working days, followed by 24 hours of weekly rest (Art. 104/105): Klacks keeps count and warns before the weekly rest is violated.

items.title: Qualifications & certifications
items.text: Shifts are only filled by staff with the right qualification — Klacks warns about expiring certifications before they become a problem.

items.title: Klacksy schedules by voice
items.text: “Schedule the weekend, two servers are out sick” is enough — Klacksy recalculates everything.

items.title: Absences covered fast
items.text: If someone drops out, Klacks immediately shows who's qualified, available, and within rest-period and maximum-working-time limits.
